questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Paraguay?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Paraguay on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Paraguay article.

questions.proof: It is bordered to the North and East by Brazil, the West by Bolivia, and the South and Southeast by Argentina.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Paraguay?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Paraguay article.

questions.proof: The main languages are Spanish and Guaraní.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It gained land in the Chaco War against _____ in the 1930s.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “against”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Paraguay article.

questions.proof: It gained land in the Chaco War against Bolivia in the 1930s.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “From 1865-1870 Paraguay lost land and most of its male population in the War of the Triple Alliance against _____, Argentina, and Uruguay.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “against”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Paraguay article.

questions.proof: From 1865-1870 Paraguay lost land and most of its male population in the War of the Triple Alliance against Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Paraguay was a colony of Spain, but became independent in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Paraguay article.

questions.proof: Paraguay was a colony of Spain, but became independent in 1811.
